### 1 — Scene
A cooked breakfast-style meal: scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage pieces, potatoes, and a small salad.

### 2 — Vessel
A square dinner plate, approximately **26 cm across**. Using the requested circular approximation:
**Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².**

### 3 — Items
Visible foods appear to be scrambled eggs, bacon, sausages, roasted potatoes, leafy greens, shredded carrot, and tomato pieces. The greens have a slight sheen, suggesting a little oil or dressing.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
Areas below partition the visible food footprint; they do not count overlapping foods twice. Bulk density is the only volume-to-weight reduction.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = volume | Density (g/ml) | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Scrambled eggs | 30% | 159 × 1.3 = 207 ml | 0.95 | 196 g | 170 | 333 kcal |
| Bacon | 14% | 74 × 0.75 = 56 ml | 0.90 | 50 g | 500 | 250 kcal |
| Sausage pieces | 12% | 64 × 1.5 = 96 ml | 0.95 | 91 g | 290 | 264 kcal |
| Roasted potatoes | 10% | 53 × 1.8 = 95 ml | 0.65 | 62 g | 150 | 93 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 12% | 64 × 2 = 128 ml | 0.15 | 19 g | 20 | 4 kcal |
| Shredded carrot | 2% | 11 × 0.7 = 8 ml | 0.60 | 4 g | 41 | 2 kcal |

**Coverage check: 30 + 14 + 12 + 10 + 12 + 2 + 5 = 85%.**  
*The dressing coats the greens, so it adds no separate footprint. Cooking fat in the other foods is included in their energy densities.*

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **450 g and 980 kcal** is plausible for this mostly covered dinner plate. Eggs make up the largest portion; bacon and sausage contribute much of the energy. The salad components receive relatively small weights.
